title: Copper's Rally Is a Supply Story, Not a Demand One
section_path: Copper's Rally Is a Supply Story, Not a Demand One
section_path_text: Copper's Rally Is a Supply Story, Not a Demand One
summary:
Main
By Ulf Bergman
Copper prices have often been seen as bellwethers for the global economy. The material's central role in modern manufacturing drives demand and, as such, influences market pricing. Against that background, current prices suggest that the global economy is facing sunlit uplands in the near term.

children.title: High but Volatile Copper Prices
children.summary: The main copper futures are currently trading well above where they began the year. At the London Metal Exchange, the three-month futures are around seventeen per cent higher than at the beginning of the year, while the October High Grade Comex contracts trade around fifteen per cent above the levels seen at the end of December.

children.title: Seaborne Copper Volumes Under Pressure
children.summary: During the year's first eight months, data from Signal Ocean show that global seaborne exports of copper concentrates declined by 10.8 per cent compared with the same period in 2025. The low shipping volumes have been a theme for much of the year, with only February exceeding volumes a year earlier.

children.title: Seaborne Volumes Supportive to Prices
children.summary: The soft seaborne export volumes for copper concentrates suggest copper prices will remain high in the coming months. While inventories may give smelters the opportunity to benefit from high prices, the increasingly soft numbers in recent months indicate that a drawdown may already be underway.
